name: Sensphere
seen: The logo is an S inside a circle with the word Sensphere in a rounded sans, in purple.
The first screen is a dark photo of a child's hands writing with a pencil, with a frosted-glass card holding the headline and two buttons, and a second glass strip of three tick points.
One strong violet is used for the top banner, buttons, logo and links, and the nav button has a violet glow.
Below the hero the page is white and very pale lavender; the How we help section has a faint dot-grid behind it.
Cards are very rounded with soft shadows; chips are pills; icons sit in small rounded squares.

Home runs: booking banner (currently booking for November 2026), hero, credentials (HCPC, RCOT, two universities), DBS and ICO badges, How we help (three cards), a comparison with NHS waiting lists, how it works, who we help, why families and schools choose.
The About page has a real photograph of the founder, Cherif Larbaoui, with a first-person account of his training.
The Pricing page shows no prices: it describes an initial assessment and a full assessment, each with Enquire for a quote, plus payment and cancellation terms.
check: Home says reports are typically ready within 10 to 15 working days; the Pricing page says a summary is typically shared within 10 working days. These may be different documents, but a parent would read them as inconsistent.
The child's hands in the hero photo: it is not known whether this is a stock photo or a real child, or whether consent exists.
The badges (DBS enhanced checked, ICO registration number) and credentials are client claims to confirm.
A small boxed character appears after Services in the menu. It may be a missing symbol in the capture browser.
The cookie card was left open at the bottom.
